provenance.accuracy: JPL's published nominal error for the Table 2a+2b fit for Jupiter over 3000 BC-AD 3000 is about 600 arcsec in heliocentric longitude, 100 arcsec in latitude, and 1,000,000 km in distance (approx_pos.html accuracy table); that figure assumes the Table 2b mean-anomaly correction is applied. This app implements Table 2a only, so actual errors are larger. Table 2b for Jupiter is b=-0.00012452, c=0.06064060, s=-0.35635438, f=38.35125000 (deg), added to the mean anomaly as b*T^2 + c*cos(f*T) + s*sin(f*T), T in centuries past J2000. Omitting it leaves an uncorrected periodic term of amplitude sqrt(c^2+s^2) = ~0.361 deg (~1300 arcsec) at any epoch, plus a secular term b*T^2 that grows from 0 at J2000 to about -0.012 deg (~45 arcsec) at the AD 3000 end of the validity window and about -0.31 deg (~1120 arcsec) at the 3000 BC end. This is a derived estimate from the Table 2b coefficients themselves, not a directly quoted 'Table-2a-only' error figure from JPL. Combined with the periodic term, the worst-case omitted correction to Jupiter's mean anomaly is on the order of 0.5-0.7 deg (roughly 1800-2500 arcsec) near the ends of the 3000 BC-AD 3000 window, translating to an along-track position error of several million km at Jupiter's ~5.2 AU heliocentric distance - well outside the 600 arcsec / 1,000,000 km budget that assumes 2b is included, and the dominant source of error in this record's orbit model. Rotation is the secular linear IAU model only (BODY599_POLE_RA/POLE_DEC/PM secular terms); the PCK's BODY599_NUT_PREC_RA/DEC/PM periodic nutation-precession terms (angles Ja-Je) are omitted, per the app's iau-linear model. The albedo triple [0.52, 0.52, 0.52] is a flat split of the single published scalar geometric albedo (0.52) across the three channels, not a per-channel measurement; the shipped Mars record does the same. The texture is a colour map, not a photometric measurement, and does not carry the albedo: the flat albedo above is what the Lambert model scales.
provenance.attribution: JPL Solar System Dynamics (orbit elements, V(1,0), geometric albedo); NSSDC Jupiter Fact Sheet (equatorial radius, polar radius, ellipticity, GM); NAIF / IAU Working Group on Cartographic Coordinates and Rotational Elements (rotation, via pck00011.tpc current BODY599 values); Solar System Scope / INOVE (texture).
provenance.coverage: Heliocentric Jupiter over 3000 BC to AD 3000 for the orbit model; rotation model validity window matched to the same span for catalogue consistency. The jupiter-2k texture ships with the app; the record falls back to a flat albedo if it is ever absent.
